analysis.rationale: Decisive overlooked evidence: (1) R0 (pointwise gamma + saturation) cannot be the true family - clean/255 pure-white pixels are mapped to a wide distribution (pair1: 12078 identical (255,255,255) pixels -> target 10-90th pct 165-246, std 32, channel means 213/207.6/203.6), which no pointwise function can produce; and all 5 targets contain exactly zero channel values at 255 while clean pair1 has 1.778% and pair3 1.474% exact 255, so the chain must spatially mix/kill highlights. (2) Wavelet sigma 0.74-1.24 (R0's reason for rejecting noise) is a blur artifact: gaussian_RGB noise sev4 (sigma=0.2*255=51) followed by blur_gaussian sev3 (sigma=3) leaves wavelet sigma ~0.1-0.25 yet its blurred field is amplified by HSV S x6 into the target's dense chroma speckle (pair0 clean chroma 9.06 -> target 33.84; satHV2 alone reaches only x1.94). (3) Pair3 (dark star trails) variance_ratio 0.362 cannot be produced by pointwise saturation alone (0.79 without blur); blur sigma3 + saturation gives 0.351-0.362 exactly. (4) The global darkening is produced by saturation min-channel clipping, not by a gamma/brightness step: satHV2 reproduces content-dependent mean shifts (pair0 -32.6 vs -34.7; pair1 -52.2 vs -53.1) and pct0 (4.0% vs 4.04%; 26.8% vs 26.78%). (5) The order noise(priority 0) -> blur(priority 1) -> saturation(priority 2) is exactly the physical order enforced by the challenge generator. R0's composite was never directly simulated; its simulation now scores 14.0-16.4 dB and creates 28% 255-clipping absent from every target.
